passage: Many learners believe that highlighting passages and rereading textbooks are the most effective ways to prepare for an exam. Because these passive techniques feel smooth and familiar, they create a powerful illusion of mastery. However, cognitive psychologists have repeatedly demonstrated that durable learning requires effortful retrieval rather than passive review. When students close their books and actively test themselves—whether through flashcards, practice questions, or explaining concepts aloud—they strengthen neural pathways and expose hidden gaps in their understanding. Although retrieval practice initially feels slower and more frustrating than simply reviewing notes, that very difficulty is what signals the brain to consolidate memories for the long term.
